title: LLMs Do Not See Age: Assessing Demographic Bias in Automated Systematic Review Synthesis

model.params_source: paper Appendix A Table 5 (temperature 0, max tokens 750); top_p assumed

task.subset_rule: paper-defined: the 15 child-group systematic reviews (PMIDs in the repo file 'reviews (2).txt')
task.approximation: Primary-study abstracts must be re-fetched from PubMed/PMC via each review's reference list (Sec. 3.1); the exact study sets are not released; prompt placement (system vs user) and abstract concatenation format are not stated; BERTScore settings not stated.

items.source: github.com/Favour-Yahdii/lllms_dont_see_age ('reviews (2).txt' lists 14 adult / 15 child / 15 older-adult review PMIDs; code only) + PubMed E-utilities for abstracts

fields.input: concatenated abstracts of the primary studies cited by the review
fields.label: the review's published abstract (PubMed)

items.license: unknown (LICENSE file present in the repo)

prompt.system: You are an experienced and objective biomedical systematic reviewer. Your task is to draft a concise, structured abstract that approximates a systematic review abstract, using the set of provided biomedical research abstracts. Ensure to produce your summary abstract based only on the provided abstracts. Do not include any external information or personal opinions. Your summary should be a synthesis of the provided abstracts, not a critique or evaluation of them.

placeholders.abstracts: the review's primary-study abstracts concatenated (format not stated)

prompt.source_location: Table 3 (regular prompt = the printed text without the bold age-aware sentence)
prompt.verbatim: full (regular prompt; its placement as system prompt with the abstracts as the user turn is an assumption)

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: BERTScore F1 between the generated abstract and the published review abstract, mean over the 15 child reviews
metric.original_location: Table 4, Regular Prompt, Child, row GPT, column BERT

open_points: no hook: the per-review primary-study abstract sets are not released and would have to be rebuilt from each review's PubMed reference list (E-utilities, ~30 abstracts x 15 reviews) - the study sets themselves are the authors' unpublished selection.
no hook: BERTScore F1 needs a roberta-large scorer (torch/transformers), outside the stdlib+numpy budget of a hook; the model/rescaling settings are also unstated.
prompt placement (system vs user) and the abstract concatenation format are not stated.
notes: Inputs are long (~30 abstracts per review, ~10k tokens) but gpt-4.1-nano is cheap; the age-aware row (0.84) and the entity metrics (ERS/HP/omission, Appendix C pipeline) are alternatives.
